tagline: Six miles of back roads from Keeneland to Old Frankfort Pike.
intro: Van Meter Road leaves Versailles Road west of Lexington, and Rice and Elkchester roads carry it on to Old Frankfort Pike, a little over six miles in all. They form part of the boundary of the West Fayette County Rural Historic District, and one house on Elkchester Road, the William Conant House, is on the National Register by itself.

The race track at the Versailles Road end keeps its old ways. It was the last track in North America to call its races over the public-address system, and did not begin until 1997. Hollywood shot most of the racing in Seabiscuit there, partly for its retro feel.

moments.title: Keeneland
moments.text: The track began in 1935 on 147 acres sold by Jack Keene, whose family had held the land for five generations, and has held its race meets in April and October since 1936.

moments.title: Manchester Farm
moments.text: On Keeneland's northern boundary, the barn with blue-and-white cupolas belongs to a farm first called Manchester Springs Plantation, after the creek that runs through it.

moments.title: Old Frankfort Pike
moments.text: At the far end the roads meet the old pike to Frankfort, lined for miles with dry-laid limestone fences.
